data.title: Token
data.tagline: A small piece of text or code that a model reads and writes
data.learningOutcome: You can recognize a token as a model-specific text piece rather than a fixed word or character.
data.description: Models split text, punctuation, and code into tokens using their own rules. Input and output token counts affect available context, wait time, and cost; a token is not always one word or one character.

learning.assumes: You have seen a chat input and a long answer.
learning.outcome: You can recognize a token as a model-specific text piece rather than a fixed word or character.

explanation.title: Split into rule-based pieces
explanation.text: The model breaks sentences into tokens using its tokenizer. English is roughly 1 token per word; Chinese is around 1.5–2 tokens per character.

explanation.title: Generated piecewise, counted both ways
explanation.text: It reads input pieces and generates output pieces one at a time. Both your prompt and the generated response count toward token usage.

explanation.title: Keep files relevant to protect quality and budget
explanation.text: A webpage's source is roughly 2,000–5,000 tokens. Sending only relevant files instead of entire projects saves cost and avoids diluting model focus.

data.boundary: One Chinese character is not guaranteed to be one token. Use the target model’s tokenizer for an exact count.

lessonPractice.title: A team estimates context and cost with one Chinese character equals one token, but bills never match. How should usage be estimated?

options.label: Use the selected model's tokenizer or actual usage for input, output, and included context
options.feedback: Tokenization varies by model and content, so actual usage or the matching tokenizer is more reliable than character rules.

options.label: Keep counting each character, letter, and punctuation mark as one token
options.feedback: Characters and tokens are not one-to-one; code, Chinese, and English may all split differently.

options.label: Count only the final AI answer and ignore system rules, history, and files
options.feedback: Input read by the model also consumes context and usage, not only newly displayed output.

data.agentPrompt: Report input, output, and cached tokens for the current model, including system rules, history, files, and tool results in input. Do not convert directly from character count; explain context usage and the cost basis.
